name: Lumen Adaptive Croptop
description:
A fitted crop top in a fabric threaded with photochromic filaments — the base color is a soft dove grey in low light, but in direct light or UV exposure the woven pattern activates: a shifting geometric design derived from Andean textile traditions, rendered in slow-moving amber and copper tones that fade back when the light drops. The effect is subtle rather than garish — a slow bloom rather than a flash. Cut short at the waist, with a wide scoop neck and minimal construction.

Lumen is a Tier 3 street-adjacent label that sits exactly between club fashion and everyday wear. The Adaptive Croptop is their signature piece — worn by people who want something that rewards attention without demanding it. It pairs easily with high-waisted trousers or layered under an open jacket. The photochromic effect doesn't require power — it's purely reactive to ambient light, which means no charging, no failure states, and no tech registration requirements.
functionality: Photochromic reactive pattern activates in direct or UV light — shifts from grey to amber/copper geometric design. No power source required.
what_it_says: I know exactly how interesting I am.
story_hooks: The photochromic pattern activates unexpectedly in a restricted area — the security cameras flag the movement pattern as a signal, and suddenly the wearer is being questioned.
A Lumen employee is quietly selling the photochromic thread formula to a corporate competitor — the next season's Stratum line has a suspiciously similar feature.
Someone wearing this shirt is the only person visible in footage of a crime scene — but the pattern makes their build and skin tone impossible to accurately determine.

physical_description.visual_profile: A minimalist fitted crop top that hits at the natural waist, creating a clean horizontal line across the torso. The silhouette is deliberately understated until light activation reveals a slow-shifting geometric pattern inspired by Andean weaving. Worn by someone moving between streetside clubs and day-shift work.
physical_description.fit: Fitted through the torso with enough stretch for breathing and movement. The wide scoop neck sits low but not dramatically — accessible for layering. Crop length is precise, not oversized.
physical_description.primary_material: Photochromic synthetic blend woven with conductive filament threads that respond to UV and direct light without requiring power. Soft hand-feel, moisture-wicking base layer construction.
physical_description.texture: Smooth and fluid in low light; the woven photochromic threads create subtle texture variation when activated. The pattern emerges gradually rather than sharply — almost imperceptible unless you're watching for it.
physical_description.color_scheme: Base: dove grey in ambient/indoor light. Activation pattern: amber and copper geometric designs (Andean-inspired tessellations) that bloom under UV or direct sunlight, then fade back to grey as light drops. No high-contrast graphics.
physical_description.closures: None — slip-on construction. The wide scoop neck provides easy dressing without fastenings.
distinctive_features: Photochromic filament threading woven throughout (no power requirement)
Deliberately subtle light-response (slow bloom, not flash)
Clean minimalist cut with no structural seams or panels
Moisture-wicking interior for club and transit wear
No visible branding — Lumen's identity is the tech itself
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 — affordable street fashion with accessible tech. Expensive enough to signal style-awareness, cheap enough for regular wear. No corpo exclusivity.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by people who move between underground club scenes and day employment. Appeals to those who want personalization without registration or power-dependency. Signals: creative, tech-comfortable, culturally aware, bridge between formal and informal economies.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine to broken-in. The photochromic effect is durable — no fading expected over normal wear. May show minor wear at scoop neck after 6+ months. Usually kept clean since the effect is the whole point.

image_prompt: Cyberpunk fashion photograph of a fitted dove-grey crop top on a model with mixed-heritage features, positioned in a club vestibule lit by neon strip lights and afternoon sun. The photochromic pattern is mid-bloom — warm amber and copper Andean geometric tessellations slowly activating across the torso in response to mixed UV and direct light. Wide scoop neck, minimal styling, high-waisted black trousers visible below. Moody side-lighting emphasizes the textile detail and the slow color shift.
